title: Oman Launches Free 14-Day Tourist Visa for 103 Countries — Here's What Indian Travelers Need to Know
excerpt: The sultanate's amended residence regulations open visa-free entry for over a hundred nationalities, but Indian passport holders must meet specific conditions to qualify for the two-week stay.
body:
• Oman now allows citizens of 103 countries to enter visa-free for up to 14 days under amended foreign residence regulations, as part of a broader push to diversify its oil-dependent economy through tourism.
  • Indian passport holders qualify for the 14-day visa-free entry only if they hold a valid visa from the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, or a Schengen country — or reside in a GCC country with an eligible profession.
  • All visa-free visitors must carry a valid passport (six months minimum), confirmed hotel reservation, return ticket, health insurance, and proof of sufficient funds.
  • The 14-day stay cannot be extended or converted into a residence visa, and overstays incur fines of approximately OMR 10 (around ₹2,200) per day.

A Gulf State Bets on Tourism

Oman has significantly expanded its visa-free entry program, allowing citizens from 103 countries to enter the sultanate for up to 14 days without securing a visa in advance. The move comes under amended foreign residence regulations designed to boost the country's tourism sector as part of Vision 2040, Oman's blueprint for reducing dependence on oil revenues.

The policy covers nationals from all European Union member states, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Australia, China, Japan, South Korea, Russia, and dozens of other countries across Latin America, Southeast Asia, and Africa. For these nationalities, entry requires only a valid passport, confirmed hotel booking, return ticket, and proof of funds.

The expansion positions Oman alongside its Gulf neighbors — particularly the UAE and Saudi Arabia — in a regional race to attract international tourists and business travelers. Oman has earmarked billions in investment for tourism, logistics, and renewable energy projects over the coming years, and easier entry is meant to lower barriers for visitors considering the country as a destination.

What Indian Passport Holders Should Know

India falls into a separate category in Oman's visa framework. Indian citizens are not eligible for unconditional visa-free entry. Instead, they qualify for the 14-day visa-free stay only under specific conditions:

They must hold a valid visa or residence permit issued by the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Japan, or a Schengen-area country. Alternatively, Indian nationals residing in a Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member state — the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, or Kuwait — may enter visa-free if their profession is among those eligible for a GCC resident visa.

"The visa exemption is subject to specific requirements to facilitate the entry of foreigners into the Sultanate. The husband, wife, and children benefit from this facility, regardless of their nationality."

— Oman's Foreign Ministry, on visa-free entry conditions

For Indians who do not meet these conditions, Oman offers an e-visa system through the Royal Oman Police portal. Tourist e-visas are available for 10-day stays (OMR 5, approximately ₹1,100) or 30-day stays (OMR 20, approximately ₹4,400), with processing times of one to three business days.

Entry Requirements and Fine Print

All visa-free visitors — regardless of nationality — must present the following at entry:

A passport valid for at least six months from the date of arrival; a confirmed hotel reservation; a return or onward flight ticket; health insurance; and proof of sufficient funds for the duration of the stay.

The 14-day period is strictly calendar-based, not calculated in 24-hour increments. Travel industry advisors warn that a late-night arrival combined with a trip spanning two calendar weeks could push travelers past the limit. The stay cannot be extended, and it cannot be converted into any type of residence visa inside Oman.

Overstay penalties are approximately OMR 10 per day. During special circumstances — such as the regional airspace disruptions in early 2026 — Oman's Royal Oman Police has waived overstay fines for stranded travelers, but this is not standard practice.

Why Oman Is Relevant for the Indian Traveler

Oman has long been a quieter alternative to Dubai for Indian travelers, offering dramatic landscapes — the Wahiba Sands desert, the fjords of Musandam, the historic forts of Nizwa — without the crowds and expense of the UAE's commercial hubs. Muscat, the capital, combines old-world Arabian architecture with modern infrastructure, and Salalah in the south draws visitors during the khareef monsoon season.

For Indians in the Gulf — one of the world's largest expatriate communities — the visa-free entry is particularly significant. An estimated 7.4 million Indians live across the six GCC countries, and Oman's proximity makes it a natural weekend or short-break destination. For those with valid US, UK, or Schengen visas — common among the professional and business-traveler segment — the removal of an additional visa requirement eliminates a real friction point.

The family benefit clause is also notable: spouses and children of eligible travelers qualify for visa-free entry regardless of their own nationality, simplifying travel planning for mixed-nationality families common in the Indian diaspora.
nri_angle: For the 7.4 million Indians living in GCC countries, Oman's visa-free entry removes a key barrier for weekend getaways, while Indians with US/UK/Schengen visas gain hassle-free access.
